title: Pressure Press
pages: Build the crusher, crush raw copper into grit, then fire the grit in a kiln to make annealed copper. Fire an iron block into eight steel billets and quench two of them with water in a quench vat to make tempered steel. The controller's own craft gate has grown as later t2 devices came online: it needs a Swaged Fitting (top-left, from the Swage Press), Tempered Steel (top-center) and a Temper Glyph (top-right), Tempered Steel either side of the center Piston, then a Riveted Brace (from the Hydraulic Riveter), a Press Drive Train and a second Swaged Fitting along the bottom row. The Flange, Crimp and Broach Presses are built in this tier but their parts are required later by the Magnetizer, Induction Coiler and Arc Press. The Temper Glyph is the tier's required magic step: hold two Annealed Copper on an Astral Font storing at least 80 night-sky lumen to consecrate them; no machine makes the glyph, so keep a sky-exposed font charged before the pressing tier. Ordinary copper ingots, plain steel billets or bare substitutes for any gate item cannot bypass these checks.

The Press Drive Train is the rotating support between the piston ram and the frame. Craft 8 Copper Grit and 1 Tin Grit into 9 Bronze Powder Blend (the 89:11 ratio of oil-retaining bearing bronze), then hot-press 2 blend into one Sintered Bronze Bushing in the Copper Hot Press (120 ticks, 8 FE/t). Stack Tempered Steel, a Swaged Fitting collar and Tempered Steel vertically to make a Drive Shaft: the shaft must be quenched and tempered because it carries torsion and fatigue load, so plain steel billets are refused. The ram needs stored rotation, so the train also carries a flywheel: place four Heavy Weighted Pressure Plates (the Copper Hot Press makes two from an iron block) around a Cast Fitting hub from the Mold Caster to craft a Flywheel Rim Blank, then quench it in the Quench Vat with 500 mB water (160 ticks, 12 FE/t). The heated rim shrinks onto the hub, giving a Shrink-Fit Flywheel; an unquenched blank is loose and is refused. Finally place Bushing, Shaft, Bushing down the left column with the Shrink-Fit Flywheel beside the top bushing for the Drive Train. The bushing and flywheel steps can be automated by hoppering blend into the hot press, or blanks and water into the Quench Vat, and extracting below. The Press also compacts 3 Bronze Powder Blend into a Green Gear Compact (100 ticks, 6 FE/t); the Copper Hot Press sinters it into the gear for the Milling Gantry's Spindle Gearbox. The Press also squeezes 8 seeds (any forge:seeds item) into one Lubricating Oil (160 ticks, 10 FE/t), the oil-bath fill that the Spindle Gearbox needs. Hopper seeds from a farm into the top to automate it.

Place materials in the left slot and take compacted blocks from the right. Use Crank or shift-right-click with an empty hand to supply 80 FE at a time, or attach Forge energy. Most pressing recipes draw 8 FE per tick; the part recipes above list their own rate (6 or 10 FE/t). The press pauses when output is full or power is absent. For the Tier 3 Signal Imprinter, press two Armor Delaminator Laminated Shells into one Transformer Core (160 ticks, 10 FE/t). Import shells above and extract the core below. For the Induction Coiler, one light weighted pressure plate made from two silver ingots is stamped into two Silver Contact Blanks (100 ticks, 8 FE/t). Feed plates from above and extract the pair below; the contact assembly then uses both blanks.

The press compacts 21 bulk materials into storage or building blocks, and its hot platen sinters four quartz, nether brick, sand or red sand straight into smooth quartz, cracked nether bricks, smooth sandstone or smooth red sandstone (120 ticks, 10 FE/t), skipping the furnace pass. Its 4-to-1 and 9-to-1 conversions preserve material quantities when blocks are unpacked. Four brick items press into one bricks block; washing four blocks returns sixteen clay balls, exactly the cost of annealing sixteen bricks. Power provides automation rather than free materials. Felting is the exception: three strings press into one white wool, one fewer than the crafting grid, and carding returns exactly three strings, so no loop gains material. Craft an iron block with two charcoal into a carburized iron charge and fire it in the kiln at 900 heat for 200 ticks to make eight steel billets. The plate is sealed by a simplified hot-dip galvanizing step: craft four billets with one zinc ingot (any forge:ingots/zinc) into four galvanizing charges, fire each at 500 heat for 80 ticks so the zinc melts over the bar as a Galvanized Steel Billet, then press it for 120 ticks and 960 FE into a sealed steel plate. A bare steel billet is not accepted, because the zinc coat is what seals the plate against rust. Keep these plates for the chemical tier. The bulk results are normal Minecraft blocks and can be unpacked where vanilla permits. Three stamping rows beat hand crafting: one iron ingot rolls into three iron bars (a table needs six ingots for sixteen), three sugar cane crush into four sugar, and eight snowballs press into one ice block.

Top and horizontal faces accept input by default; bottom exports output. Six menu buttons cycle Off, In and Out per world face. Ports, FE, inventory and work survive saves; breaking drops the input and result. The press has its own datapack recipe type, arcana_industry:pressing, with ingredient, count, result, duration, energy_per_tick and optional priority. JEI shows the recipes and the press catalyst when installed.
Press two leather hides for 120 ticks at 8 FE/t into a compact friction lining. Move it from the bottom output port to the clutch craft; a loose hide will not hold the drum clutch.

For the Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchanger, stamp one Tool Steel Stock into four Tab Lock Washers (120 ticks, 8 FE/t). Feed stock through the top input and extract washers below. The bent tabs hold two head-flange bolts against vibration; a plain bolt set does not replace a washer in the exchanger craft. JEI lists this pressing recipe and the Pressure Press catalyst.

Stamp two Sealed Steel Plates into one Stamped Contactor Enclosure in the powered Pressure Press (140 ticks, 10 FE/t). This one-piece box leaves a recessed space for the switching contacts and shielded wiring. Feed plates through an input face and extract the enclosure from the output face. JEI lists the pressing input, batch size and power cost.

Emboss one Seam Press Clamped Liner in the powered Pressure Press (140 ticks, 10 FE/t) into an Embossed Wear Liner. The pressed channels give the Leaching Vat a replaceable abrasion surface. Hopper clamped liners into an input face and extract the result below. JEI shows this pressing recipe and its power cost.
